edits.section: Intro, paragraph 1 (states plainly that there is no headline figure, and why)
edits.old: A single figure blends all of those together and says very little about your own wedding.
edits.new: A single figure blends all of those together and says very little about your own wedding, so this guide gives no headline figure: the total depends on those drivers, and one written brief sent to several venues gets you a real number.

edits.section: What shapes the cost > Exclusive use (closed to the public, as a question)
edits.old: Ask, too, whether another wedding can be held there the same day.
edits.new: Ask, too, whether another wedding can be held there the same day, and whether the property can stay closed to the public for the whole celebration.

edits.section: What shapes the cost > Guest numbers (event size, as a question)
edits.old: Ask which items are charged per guest, whether there is a minimum spend for your date, and when the final number is locked.
edits.new: Ask which items are charged per guest, whether there is a minimum spend for your date, and when the final number is locked. For a large guest list, ask what size of event the venue has hosted.

edits.section: What shapes the cost > The legal route and its fees, paragraph 2 (Rhodes made a worked example; split into a short list, all markers kept)
edits.old: Rhodes shows what a civil wedding involves. The Municipality of Rhodes lists a joint application, a certificate of no impediment to marriage naming the person you will marry, passport copies, a form with your details and a municipal fee. <!-- fact_01 --> Documents issued abroad must be recent originals, officially translated into Greek, and those from outside the European Union need an Apostille. <!-- fact_02 --> Originals go to the registrar two days before the wedding, and a fee applies at the registry office. <!-- fact_04 -->
edits.new:
Rhodes is the worked example, because its municipality publishes the list. On another island, ask that municipality for its own.

- **The application:** a joint application, a certificate of no impediment to marriage naming the person you will marry, passport copies, a form with your details and a municipal fee. <!-- fact_01 -->
- **Documents from abroad:** recent originals, officially translated into Greek, with an Apostille on those from outside the European Union. <!-- fact_02 -->
- **Before the day:** originals go to the registrar two days before the wedding, and a fee applies at the registry office. <!-- fact_04 -->

edits.section: What shapes the cost > The legal route and its fees, paragraph 3 (Australian documents as two short points, markers kept)
edits.old: The [Australian Embassy in Athens](https://greece.embassy.gov.au/athn/notarial.html) issues certificates of no impediment and applies apostilles to original Australian public documents, and a fee applies. <!-- fact_06 --> <!-- fact_07 --> DFAT also legalises Australian documents for a fee, with slower processing in peak holiday periods. <!-- fact_18 --> <!-- fact_19 -->
edits.new:
For the Australian documents:

- The [Australian Embassy in Athens](https://greece.embassy.gov.au/athn/notarial.html) issues certificates of no impediment and applies apostilles to original Australian public documents, for a fee. <!-- fact_06 --> <!-- fact_07 -->
- DFAT also legalises Australian documents for a fee, and processing is slower in peak holiday periods. <!-- fact_18 --> <!-- fact_19 -->

edits.section: FAQ > Is it expensive to have a wedding in Greece? (honest contrast from the draft, not a shrug)
edits.old: It depends on the wedding you plan. Island, venue, season, guest numbers and guest travel all move the total.
edits.new: It can be either. A town hall ceremony with lunch for close family and a clifftop weekend with ferries for every guest sit at very different ends. Island, venue, season, guest numbers and guest travel decide where yours lands.

edits.section: FAQ > How much does a wedding in Greece cost? (says plainly why there is no headline figure and how to get a real one)
edits.old: The total depends on the drivers above: island and venue, date, guest list, legal route, the events across the weekend and what you cover for guests. Ask each venue to quote against the same written brief, then compare line by line.
edits.new: This guide gives no headline figure, because no single number holds until your island, venue, date, guest list, legal route and guest travel are set. For a real one, send each venue the same written brief, then compare the written quotes line by line.
